title.raw: 卷22 孝文五王 Volume 22: Emperor Xiaowen's Five Princes

sentences.zh: 孝文皇帝七男：林皇后生廢太子恂。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen had seven sons: Empress Lin bore Xun, the Deposed Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen had seven sons: Empress Lin bore Xun, the Deposed Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 文昭皇后生宣武皇帝、廣平文穆王懷。

translations.literal: Empress Wenzhao bore Emperor Xuanwu and Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenzhao bore Emperor Xuanwu and Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 袁貴人生京兆王愉。

translations.literal: Noble Lady Yuan bore Yu, Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Lady Yuan bore Yu, Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 羅夫人生清河文獻王懌、汝南文宣王悅。

translations.literal: Lady Luo gave birth to Prince of Qinghe, posthumous Wenxian Yi, and Prince of Runan, posthumous Wenzuan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Luo bore Yi, Prince of Qinghe (posthumous Wenxian), and Yue, Prince of Runan (posthumous Wenzuan).

sentences.zh: 鄭充華生皇子恌，未封，早夭。

translations.literal: Zheng Chonghua bore the prince Ti; he was not enfeoffed and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chonghua bore the prince Ti, who was never enfeoffed and died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 廢太子庶人恂，字元道。

translations.literal: The Deposed Crown Prince, the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Crown Prince Xun, reduced to commoner rank, styled Yuandao.

sentences.zh: 生而母死，文明太后撫視之，常置左右。

translations.literal: At birth his mother died; Empress Dowager Wenming raised and watched over him, always keeping him at her side.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was born; Empress Dowager Wenming reared him and kept him constantly at her side.

sentences.zh: 年四歲，太皇太后親為立名恂，字元道，於是大赦。

translations.literal: At age four the Grand Empress Dowager personally established his name Xun, styled Yuandao, and thereupon a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was four the Grand Empress Dowager herself named him Xun, styled Yuandao, and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: [3]太和十七年七月癸丑，立恂為皇太子。

translations.literal: [3] In the seventh month of Taihe year seventeen, on day guichou, Xun was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: [3] In the seventh month of Taihe year 17, on the day guichou, Xun was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及冠恂於廟，高祖臨光極東堂，引恂入見，誡以冠義曰：「夫冠禮表之百代，所以正容體，齊顏色，順辭令。

translations.literal: At his capping in the ancestral temple Gaozu sat in the east hall of the Guangji Palace, drew Xun in to see him, and admonished him on the meaning of the cap, saying: "The capping rite manifests itself to a hundred generations; by it one sets the body right, aligns the complexion, and orders one's speech.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was capped in the ancestral temple, Gaozu received him in the east hall of the Guangji Palace and taught him the meaning of the ceremony: "The capping rite stands for a hundred generations. It sets the body upright, aligns the face, and orders the tongue.

sentences.zh: 容體正，顏色齊，辭令順；

translations.literal: When the body is right, the complexion aligned, and speech in order;
translations.idiomatic: When bearing is upright, the face composed, and words measured,

sentences.zh: 故能正君臣，親父子，和長幼。

translations.literal: then lord and minister can be set right, father and son drawn close, elder and younger harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: then ruler and minister are set right, father and son brought near, and elder and younger brought into harmony.

sentences.zh: 然母見必拜，兄弟必敬，責以成人之禮。

translations.literal: Yet when he sees his mother he must bow, to his brothers he must show respect—charged with the rites of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he must bow when he sees his mother and show respect to his brothers, for he is now bound by the rites of adulthood.

sentences.zh: 字汝元道，所寄不輕。

translations.literal: Your style is Ru Yuandao; what is entrusted to you is not light.
translations.idiomatic: Your style is Ru Yuandao—what is laid upon you is no small thing.

sentences.zh: 汝當尋名求義，以順吾旨。」

translations.literal: You should seek the meaning in your name and follow my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Seek the meaning in your name and walk in accord with my intent."

sentences.zh: 二十年，改字宣道。

translations.literal: In year twenty his style was changed to Xuandao.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 his style was changed to Xuandao.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，詔恂詣代都。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict ordered Xun to proceed to the Dai capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Luoyang, Xun was ordered to go to the Dai capital.

sentences.zh: 其進止儀禮，高祖皆為定。

translations.literal: His comings and goings and ritual deportment Gaozu fixed for him in every detail.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu prescribed every detail of his movements and ceremonial bearing.

sentences.zh: 及恂入辭，高祖曰：「今汝不應向代，但太師薨於恒壤，朕既居皇極之重，不容輕赴舅氏之喪，欲使汝展哀舅氏，拜汝母墓，一寫為子之情。

translations.literal: When Xun entered to take leave Gaozu said: "Now you should not go toward Dai; but the Grand Preceptor has died at Hengrang. I, having taken up the weight of the imperial pole, cannot lightly go to my maternal uncle's mourning. I wish you to extend mourning for your maternal uncle and bow at your mother's tomb, writing out in full a son's feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun came to take leave Gaozu said, "You are not to turn toward Dai. The Grand Preceptor has died at Hengrang. I bear the weight of the throne and cannot lightly attend my uncle's mourning. Go and mourn for him in my stead, bow at your mother's tomb, and pour out there everything a son owes.

sentences.zh: 汝至彼，太師事畢後日，宜一拜山陵。

translations.literal: When you arrive there, one day after the Grand Preceptor's rites are finished you should once bow at the mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When you arrive, wait one day after the Grand Preceptor's rites are done, then bow once at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，汝族祖南安可一就問訊。

translations.literal: When the bowing is finished your clan-grandfather the Prince of Nan'an may once be approached for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: After that you may call once on your clan-grandfather, the Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 在途，當溫讀經籍。

translations.literal: On the road you should diligently read the classics.
translations.idiomatic: On the road, read the classics with steady care.

sentences.zh: 今日親見吾也。」

translations.literal: Today you see me in person."
translations.idiomatic: Today you see me face to face."

sentences.zh: [4]後高祖每歲征幸，恂常留守，主執廟祀。

translations.literal: [4] Afterward, whenever Gaozu went on campaign each year, Xun always remained to guard the capital and preside over temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Thereafter, whenever Gaozu marched out each year, Xun stayed behind to guard the capital and preside over the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 恂不好書學，體貌肥大，深忌河洛暑熱，意每追樂北方。

translations.literal: Xun did not love literary study; his body was large and fat; he deeply dreaded the heat of the He-Luo region; his mind always yearned for the pleasures of the north.
translations.idiomatic: Xun cared little for books. He was heavy of build and loathed the heat of the He-Luo basin; his heart always turned northward.

sentences.zh: 中庶子高道悅數苦言致諫，恂甚銜之。

translations.literal: The household steward Gao Daoyue repeatedly spoke bitter admonition; Xun greatly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His household steward Gao Daoyue admonished him again and again until Xun came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸崧岳，恂留守金墉，於西掖門內與左右謀，欲召牧馬輕騎奔代，手刃道悅於禁中。

translations.literal: When Gaozu visited Mount Song, Xun guarded Jinyong; within the west side gate he plotted with his attendants to summon the horse-tenders' light cavalry and flee to Dai, and with his own hand cut down Daoyue in the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was at Mount Song, Xun held Jinyong. Inside the west side gate he plotted with his attendants to call up the horse-keepers' light cavalry and flee to Dai, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 領軍元儼勒門防遏，夜得寧靜。

translations.literal: The commandant of guards Yuan Yan restrained the gates; by night all was quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of guards Yuan Yan barred the gates and held the night quiet.

sentences.zh: 厥明，尚書陸琇馳啟高祖於南，高祖聞之駭惋，外寢其事，仍至汴口而還。

translations.literal: At dawn Director of Documents Lu Diu hurried a memorial to Gaozu in the south; Gaozu, hearing it, was alarmed and grieved; outwardly he concealed the matter and still went as far as Bian mouth before returning.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Director of Documents Lu Diu sent an urgent report south. Gaozu was shaken and grieved, but outwardly he hid the affair and still rode as far as Bian mouth before turning back.

sentences.zh: 引恂數罪，與咸陽王禧等親杖恂，又令禧等更代，百餘下，扶曳出外，不起者月餘。

translations.literal: He drew out Xun's many crimes; with the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally caned Xun, and ordered Xi and the others to take turns—more than a hundred blows—and had him dragged out; for more than a month he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He recited Xun's crimes one by one. With the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally beat him, then had them take turns until more than a hundred strokes were laid on. Xun was dragged out and could not rise for over a month.

sentences.zh: 拘於城西別館。

translations.literal: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was confined in a lodge apart, west of the city.

sentences.zh: 引見羣臣於清徽堂，議廢之。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned the ministers at the Clear Emblem Hall and discussed deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned the ministers to the Clear Emblem Hall to discuss deposing him.

sentences.zh: 司空、太子太傅穆亮，尚書僕射、少保李沖，並免冠稽首而謝。

translations.literal: Director of Works and Crown Prince Grand Tutor Mu Liang, and Vice Director and Junior Tutor Li Chong, both removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Works and crown prince grand tutor Mu Liang, and vice director and junior tutor Li Chong, both removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿所謝者私也，我所議者國也。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "What you apologize for is private; what I discuss is the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "What you apologize for is a private matter. What I discuss is the state.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，大義滅親。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: great righteousness extinguishes kin.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that great righteousness may destroy one's own kin.

sentences.zh: 今恂欲違父背尊，跨據恒朔。

translations.literal: Now Xun wishes to oppose his father, turn from his superior, seize and hold Heng and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Xun now means to defy his father, abandon his rank, and seize the north at Heng and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 天下未有無父國，何其包藏，心與身俱。

translations.literal: Under Heaven there has never been a state without a father; how deep is his concealment—heart and body together.
translations.idiomatic: There is no realm without a father. How deep is his treachery—heart and deed as one.

sentences.zh: 此小兒今日不滅，乃是國家之大禍，脫待我無後，恐有永嘉之亂。」

translations.literal: If this boy today is not destroyed he is the great calamity of the state; if we wait until I have no successor, I fear there will be chaos like that of Yongjia."
translations.idiomatic: If I do not destroy this boy today, he will be the state's great ruin. If I wait until I have no heir left, I fear another Yongjia upheaval."

sentences.zh: 乃廢為庶人，置之河陽，以兵守之，服食所供，粗免飢寒而已。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was deposed to commoner rank, placed at Heyang, guarded by soldiers; food and clothing supplied barely kept off hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: He was deposed to commoner rank and sent to Heyang under guard. Food and clothing were given only enough to keep hunger and cold at bay.

sentences.zh: 恂在困躓，頗知咎悔，恒讀佛經，禮拜歸心於善。

translations.literal: Xun in his straits came somewhat to know fault and repentance; he constantly read Buddhist sutras, bowed, and turned his heart toward good.
translations.idiomatic: In his fall Xun came partly to repent. He read Buddhist sutras, bowed, and turned his heart toward what was good.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸代，遂如長安。

translations.literal: When Gaozu visited Dai he then proceeded to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu went to Dai he continued on to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 中尉李彪承間密表，告恂復與左右謀逆。

translations.literal: The commandant of palace guards Li Biao seized an interval with a secret memorial reporting that Xun again plotted rebellion with his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of palace guards Li Biao sent a secret memorial reporting that Xun was again plotting rebellion with his attendants.

sentences.zh: 高祖在長安，使中書侍郎邢巒與咸陽王禧，奉詔齎椒酒詣河陽，賜恂死，時年十五。

translations.literal: Gaozu at Chang'an sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Xing Luan with the Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict and carrying peppered wine to Heyang, and bestowed death on Xun; he was then fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an Gaozu sent palace secretariat attendant Xing Luan with the Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict and peppered wine to Heyang, and had Xun put to death. He was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 殮以粗棺常服，瘞於河陽城。

translations.literal: He was enfolded in a coarse coffin in common dress and buried in Heyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He was laid in a plain coffin in ordinary dress and buried in Heyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年冬，御史臺令史龍文觀坐法當死，告廷尉，稱恂前被攝左右之日，有手書自理不知狀，而中尉李彪、侍御史賈尚寢不為聞。

translations.literal: In the winter of year twenty-two the reviewing censor's clerk Long Wenguan, sentenced to death for violating the law, reported to the Court Commander that when Xun before was seized by his attendants he had written by hand a plea that he did not know the circumstances, yet Li Biao the commandant and attendant censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report upward.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 22 the reviewing censor's clerk Long Wenguan, condemned to death for a legal offense, told the Court Commander that when Xun was seized his attendants had found a handwritten plea that he did not know what was afoot, yet Commandant Li Biao and attendant censor Jia Shang had buried the matter and never reported it.

sentences.zh: 賈坐繫廷尉。

translations.literal: Jia was sentenced and imprisoned at the Court Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was sentenced and held at the Court Commander's office.

sentences.zh: 時彪免歸，高祖在鄴，尚書表收彪赴洛，會赦，遂不窮其本末。

translations.literal: At that time Biao had been dismissed and returned home; Gaozu was at Ye; the Director of Documents memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; they met an amnesty, and therefore the matter was not pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: By then Biao had been dismissed and gone home. Gaozu was at Ye. The secretariat memorialized to arrest Biao and send him to Luoyang, but an amnesty intervened and the case was never pursued to its roots.

sentences.zh: 賈尚出繫，暴病數日死。

translations.literal: Jia Shang was released from prison; sudden illness; within several days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Shang was released from prison, fell suddenly ill, and died within days.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖將為恂娶司徒馮誕長女，以女幼，待年長。

translations.literal: Initially Gaozu was to marry Xun to Minister of Works Feng Dan's eldest daughter; because the girl was young he waited until she came of age.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gaozu meant to marry Xun to the eldest daughter of Minister of Works Feng Dan, but because the girl was young he waited until she grew.

sentences.zh: 先為娉彭城劉長文、滎陽鄭懿女為左右孺子，時恂年十三四。

translations.literal: First he betrothed for him the daughters of Pengcheng Liu Changwen and Xingyang Zheng Yi as left and right Ruzi; at the time Xun was thirteen or fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: He first betrothed to him the daughters of Liu Changwen of Pengcheng and Zheng Yi of Xingyang as left and right concubines when Xun was thirteen or fourteen.

sentences.zh: 高祖泛舟天淵池，謂郭祚、崔光、宋弁曰：「人生須自放，不可終朝讀書。

translations.literal: Gaozu floated a boat on the Tianyuan Pool and said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian: "In life one must let oneself go; one cannot read books from morning to night.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drifted a boat on the Tianyuan Pool and said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian, "A man must sometimes loosen the rein. He cannot read from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 我欲使恂旦出省經傳，食後還內，晡時復出，日夕而罷。

translations.literal: I wish to have Xun go out in the morning to review the classics, return within after eating, go out again at the hour of shen, and stop at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to have Xun go out each morning to study the classics, return at midday, go out again in the afternoon, and be done by evening.

sentences.zh: 卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: You all take it how?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 光曰：「孔子稱：『血氣未定，戒之在色』，傳曰：『晝以訪事，夜以安身』。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Confucius said: 'When the blood and breath are not yet settled, beware of color'; the tradition says: 'By day inquire into affairs, by night rest the body.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang said, "Confucius warned, 'When blood and breath are unsettled, beware of desire.' The tradition says, 'By day attend to affairs; by night rest the body.'

sentences.zh: 太子以幼年涉學之日，不宜於正晝之時，捨書御內，又非所以安柔弱之體，固永年之命。」

translations.literal: The crown prince, in the years when he first touches learning, should not in the bright hours of day set aside his books and enter the inner quarters; this also is not how to settle a tender body and secure years of life."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is still in his first years of study. He should not in broad daylight leave his books for the inner quarters—that is no way to guard a tender frame or secure a long life."

sentences.zh: 高祖以光言為然，乃不令恂晝入內。

translations.literal: Gaozu took Guang's words as right and therefore did not let Xun enter within by day.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu accepted Guang's counsel and would not let Xun enter the inner palace by day.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉，字宣德。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Jingzhao, styled Xuande.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年封。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in Taihe year twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 21.

sentences.zh: 拜都督、徐州刺史，以彭城王中軍府長史盧陽烏兼長史，州事巨細，委之陽烏。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou; Pengcheng Wang's center-army office chief clerk Lu Yangwu was made acting chief clerk, and great and small matters of the province were entrusted to Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou. Lu Yangwu, chief clerk of the Prince of Pengcheng's center-army office, served as acting chief clerk, and every detail of the province was left to him.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made guardian general of the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shizong's reign he was made guardian general of the army.

sentences.zh: 世宗留愛諸弟，愉等常出入宮掖，晨昏寢處，若家人焉。

translations.literal: Shizong cherished his younger brothers; Yu and the others constantly went in and out of the palace women's quarters, morning and evening sleeping and dwelling as if a family household.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong doted on his younger brothers. Yu and the others moved freely through the palace quarters, sleeping and waking with him morning and evening like members of one household.

sentences.zh: 世宗每日華林戲射，衣衫騎從，往來無間。

translations.literal: Each day Shizong shot for sport in the Hualin Garden; in light dress and mounted retinue they came and went without interval.
translations.idiomatic: Every day Shizong shot for sport in the Hualin Garden, and Yu rode with him in light dress, back and forth without pause.

sentences.zh: 遷中書監。

translations.literal: Transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世宗為納順皇后妹為妃，而不見禮答。

translations.literal: Shizong married for him the younger sister of Empress Shun as consort, but Yu did not treat her with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong gave him the younger sister of Empress Shun as consort, but Yu never showed her proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 愉在徐州，納妾李氏，本姓楊，東郡人，夜聞其歌，悅之，遂被寵嬖。

translations.literal: While Yu was in Xuzhou he took a concubine, Lady Li, originally surnamed Yang, a man of Dong commandery; hearing her sing at night he was pleased and thereafter she received his favor.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu held Xuzhou he took a concubine, Lady Li—born Yang, from Dong commandery. He heard her sing one night, was delighted, and thereafter she held his favor.

sentences.zh: 罷州還京，欲進貴之，託右中郎將趙郡李恃顯為之養父，就之禮逆，產子寶月。

translations.literal: When he left the province and returned to the capital he wished to advance her rank; he entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery to act as her adoptive father, and by that rite married her; she bore the son Baoyue.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office for the capital he wished to raise her standing. He had Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery stand as her adoptive father, married her by that rite, and she bore Baoyue.

sentences.zh: 順皇后召李入宮，毀擊之，強令為尼於內，以子付妃養之。

translations.literal: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace, beat and reviled her, forced her to become a nun within, and gave the child to the consort to rear.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace, struck and abused her, forced her to take the tonsure inside, and gave the child to the consort to raise.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，后父于勁，以后久無所誕，乃上表勸廣嬪侍。

translations.literal: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long had borne no child, submitted a memorial urging that secondary consorts attend the bed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, seeing that she still bore no child, memorialized urging that secondary consorts attend the bed.

sentences.zh: 因令后歸李於愉，舊愛更甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love grew still stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was made to return Li to Yu, and his old love burned hotter than before.

sentences.zh: 愉好文章，頗著詩賦。

translations.literal: Yu loved literary composition and notably composed poetry and fu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu loved letters and wrote poetry and fu with some distinction.

sentences.zh: 時引才人宋世景、李神儁、祖瑩、邢晏、王遵業、張始均等共申宴喜，招四方儒學賓客嚴懷真等數十人，館而禮之。

translations.literal: At the time he constantly drew in talented men Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others to share feasts and joy; he recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four directions such as Yan Huaizhen, housed them, and honored them with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He often gathered men of talent—Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others—for feasts and delight, and hosted several dozen Confucian guests from across the realm, including Yan Huaizhen, treating them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 所得穀帛，率多散施。

translations.literal: The grain and silk he received he mostly dispersed in gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the grain and silk that came to him he gave away.

sentences.zh: 又崇信佛道，用度常至不接。

translations.literal: He also revered the Buddhist way; his expenses often fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoted himself to Buddhism, and his expenses often outran his income.

sentences.zh: 與弟廣平王懷頗相夸尚，競慕奢麗，貪縱不法。

translations.literal: With his younger brother the Prince of Guangping Huai he rather vied in display, emulating extravagant splendor, greedy and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: With his younger brother Huai, Prince of Guangping, he vied in display, each chasing extravagance, greedy and heedless of law.

sentences.zh: 於是世宗攝愉禁中推案，杖愉五十，出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shizong took Yu into the forbidden precinct to investigate, caned him fifty times, and sent him out as governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong then had Yu seized in the inner palace, investigated him, gave him fifty strokes, and sent him out as governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 始愉自以職求侍要，[5]既勢劣二弟，潛懷愧恨，頗見言色。

translations.literal: At first Yu himself thought that by his office he might obtain attendance on important affairs; [5] now that his power was inferior to his two younger brothers he secretly harbored shame and resentment and rather showed it in speech and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yu had believed his rank would win him a place near power; [5] finding himself weaker than his two younger brothers, he nursed secret shame and let it show in word and face.

sentences.zh: 又以幸妾屢被頓辱，內外離抑。

translations.literal: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, within and without he was estranged and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: His favored concubine had been shamed again and again, and at court and at home he was isolated and pressed down.

sentences.zh: 及在州謀逆，愉遂殺長史羊靈引及司馬李遵，稱得清河王密疏，云高肇謀殺害主上。

translations.literal: When in the province he plotted rebellion, Yu then killed chief clerk Yang Lingyin and marshal Li Zun, claiming to have received a secret letter from the Prince of Qinghe saying Gao Zhao plotted to murder the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: While he was in the province he rose in rebellion. Yu killed chief clerk Yang Lingyin and marshal Li Zun, claiming a secret letter from the Prince of Qinghe that Gao Zhao meant to murder the emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是遂為壇於信都之南，柴燎告天，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: He built an altar south of Xindu, burned offerings and declared himself to Heaven, and took the imperial title on the spot.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，號建平元年，立李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He proclaimed amnesty for all under Heaven, era name Jianping year one, and installed Lady Li as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Jianping year 1, and made Lady Li empress.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔尚書李平討愉。

translations.literal: Shizong ordered Director of Documents Li Ping to campaign against Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong ordered Director of Documents Li Ping to suppress Yu.

sentences.zh: 愉出拒王師，頻敗，遂嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then closed the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu marched out against the imperial host, was beaten again and again, and finally shut himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 愉知事窮，攜李及四子數十騎出門，諸軍追之，見執以送。

translations.literal: Yu knew the affair was exhausted; he took Li and four sons with several tens of horsemen and went out the gate; the armies pursued and seized him and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing all was lost, Yu took Li and four sons and rode out with a few dozen horsemen. The armies overtook him, seized him, and sent him in.

sentences.zh: 詔徵赴京師，申以家人之訓。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with the teaching of a family.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him as kin.

sentences.zh: 愉每止宿亭傳，必攜李手，盡其私情。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu halted at a post station he always took Li by the hand and indulged their private feeling to the full.
translations.idiomatic: At every post station Yu held Li by the hand and gave their private bond its full expression.

sentences.zh: 雖鎖縶之中，飲食自若，略無愧懼之色。

translations.literal: Though in fetters, in eating and drinking he was as before, with scarcely a shade of shame or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Even in chains he ate and drank as before, showing hardly a trace of shame or fear.

sentences.zh: 至野王，愉語人曰：「雖主上慈深，不忍殺我，吾亦何面目見於至尊！」

translations.literal: When he reached Yewang Yu said to others: "Though the sovereign's kindness is deep and he will not bear to kill me, what face have I to see the August One!"
translations.idiomatic: At Yewang Yu told those about him, "The emperor's mercy runs deep and he may spare my life—but what face have I left to show the throne?"

sentences.zh: 於是歔欷流涕，絕氣而死，年二十一。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sobbed, tears flowing; his breath broke and he died; he was then twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He wept until his breath failed and he died. He was twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 或云高肇令人殺之。

translations.literal: Some say Gao Zhao had men kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Gao Zhao had him killed.

sentences.zh: 斂以小棺，瘞之。

translations.literal: He was enfolded in a small coffin and buried.
translations.idiomatic: He was laid in a small coffin and buried.

sentences.zh: 諸子至洛，皆赦之。

translations.literal: When the sons reached Luoyang they were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons reached Luoyang they were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後靈太后令愉之四子皆附屬籍，追封愉臨洮王。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling ordered that Yu's four sons all be entered on the register of kin, and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Dowager Ling had Yu's four sons entered on the clan register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 子寶月襲。

translations.literal: The son Baoyue inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoyue inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 乃改葬父母，追服三年。

translations.literal: He then reburied his parents and observed mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He reburied his parents and observed three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 寶月弟寶炬，輕躁薄行，耽淫酒色。

translations.literal: Baoyue's younger brother Baoju was frivolous and of slight conduct, addicted to wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyue's younger brother Baoju was rash and loose in conduct, given to wine and women.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，特封南陽王。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaozhuang he was specially enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he was specially enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 從出帝沒於關西。

translations.literal: He followed the Deposed Emperor out and perished west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Deposed Emperor west of the Pass and perished there.

sentences.zh: 宇文黑獺害出帝，寶炬乃僭大號。

translations.literal: Yuwen Heituo killed the Deposed Emperor, and Baoju thereupon usurped the great title.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Heituo slew the Deposed Emperor; Yuan Baoju then seized the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌，字宣仁。

translations.literal: Prince Qinghe Yi, courtesy name Xuanren.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe Wang Yi, styled Xuanren.

sentences.zh: 幼而敏惠，美姿貌，高祖愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and quick-witted, of fine appearance; Emperor Gaozu loved him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever and handsome, and Gaozu doted on him.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰甚器異之，並曰：「此兒風神外偉，黃中內潤，若天假之年，比二南矣。」

translations.literal: Prince Pengcheng Xie greatly prized and singled him out, and together they said: "This boy's spirit and bearing are outwardly grand, his yellow core inwardly lustrous; if Heaven grants him years, he will rival the Two Souths."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng Xie prized him highly and said with others, "This child's bearing is outwardly grand and inwardly rich; given a full span of years he would rival the Two Souths."

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，兼綜羣言，有文才，善談理，寬仁容裕，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: He ranged broadly through the classics and histories, took in many schools of thought, had literary talent, was skilled at discourse on principle, generous and tolerant in bearing, and did not let joy or anger show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered classics and histories, absorbed many traditions, wrote well, argued ably, and was magnanimous—joy and anger never showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He received his fief in Taihe year 21.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，拜侍中，轉尚書僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was appointed Palace Attendant, then transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong acceded he became palace attendant, then vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 懌才長從政，明於斷決，割判眾務，甚有聲名。

translations.literal: Yi was talented and long in government; clear in judgment and decision, he sliced through the multitude of affairs and won a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yi excelled in administration, decided cases with clarity, cut through piled business, and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 司空高肇以帝舅寵任，既擅威權，謀去良宗，屢譖懌及愉等。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Gao Zhao, favored as the emperor's maternal uncle, already monopolized awesome power and plotted to remove worthy clansmen, repeatedly slandering Yi and Yu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, the emperor's uncle by marriage, already held unchecked power and sought to purge the princes, repeatedly denouncing Yi, Yu, and others.

sentences.zh: 愉不勝其忿怒，遂舉逆冀州。

translations.literal: Yu could not bear his fury and thereupon raised rebellion in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, unable to endure the pressure, rebelled in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 因愉之逆，又構殺勰。

translations.literal: Using Yu's rebellion as pretext, he also framed and killed Xie.
translations.idiomatic: He used Yu's revolt as pretext to frame and kill Xie as well.

sentences.zh: 懌恐不免。

translations.literal: Yi feared he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yi feared he would not escape.

sentences.zh: 肇又錄囚徒，以立私惠。

translations.literal: Zhao again reviewed prisoners to build private goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao again reviewed prisoners to curry private favor.

sentences.zh: 懌因侍宴酒酣，乃謂肇曰：「天子兄弟，詎有幾人，而炎炎不息。

translations.literal: At a banquet where Yi attended him, wine deep, Yi said to Zhao: "The Son of Heaven's brothers—how many are there?—yet you blaze on without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When wine had deepened at a feast Yi told Zhao, "The emperor's brothers are few—why does your flame never die down?

sentences.zh: 昔王莽頭禿，亦藉渭陽之資，遂篡漢室，今君曲形見矣，恐復終成亂階。」

translations.literal: In old times Wang Mang's head was bald, yet he still relied on kin through the empress's family and usurped the Han house; now your bent form is already plain to see—I fear you will again become the stairway of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang was bald yet rode empress-kin ties to seize the Han throne; your crooked shape is plain already—I fear you will be disorder's stair again."

sentences.zh: 又言於世宗曰：「臣聞唯器與名，不可以假人。

translations.literal: He also said to Emperor Shizong: "Your servant has heard that vessels and names may not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Shizong, "I have heard that ritual vessels and titles must not be lent away.

sentences.zh: 是故季氏旅泰，宣尼以為深譏；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Ji clan overstepped at Mount Tai, Confucius deeply censured it;
translations.idiomatic: When the Ji clan overreached at Mount Tai, Confucius censured it deeply;

sentences.zh: 仲叔軒懸，丘明以為至誡。

translations.literal: when Zhongsun hung his drums as for a lord, Qiu Ming took it as the utmost warning.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhongsun's house displayed lordly drums, Qiu Ming called it the gravest warning.

sentences.zh: 諒以天尊地卑，君臣道別，宜杜漸防萌，無相僭越。

translations.literal: Truly heaven is honored and earth is lowly—the way of ruler and minister is distinct; one should stop the first sprout and guard against encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is high and earth low; ruler and minister are separate—one must nip usurpation in the bud.

sentences.zh: 至於減膳錄囚，人君之事，今乃司徒行之，詎是人臣之義？

translations.literal: As for reducing meals and reviewing prisoners—these are a ruler's affairs; now the Minister of Works performs them—how is that the meaning of a subject?
translations.idiomatic: Reducing meals and reviewing prisoners belong to the ruler; for the minister of works to do them—what subject's duty is that?

sentences.zh: 且陛下修政教，解獄訟，則時雨可降，玉燭知和，何使明君失之於上，姦臣竊之於下。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty reforms government and teaching and releases prisoners from litigation—then timely rain may descend and the jade candle know harmony; why let an enlightened ruler lose them above while treacherous ministers steal them below?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reforms rule and clears suits, timely rain and harmony follow—why let the wise ruler lose these above while traitors seize them below?

sentences.zh: 長亂之基，於此在矣。」

translations.literal: The root of long disorder lies here."
translations.idiomatic: The root of lasting disorder is here."

sentences.zh: 世宗笑而不應。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong smiled and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，遷太尉，侍中如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was transferred to Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's accession he was made grand marshal while remaining palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔懌裁門下之事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi to decide affairs of the Gate and Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Gate-and-Chamber business in Yi's hands.

sentences.zh: 又典經義注。

translations.literal: He also oversaw annotated classics.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed classical annotation.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門惠憐者，自云呪水飲人，能差諸病。

translations.literal: At the time there was a monk named Huilian who claimed that charmed water given to drink could cure all illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: A monk Huilian claimed his charmed water cured every illness.

sentences.zh: 病人就之者，日有千數。

translations.literal: Those who came to him sick numbered thousands a day.
translations.idiomatic: Sick people flocked to him by the thousand each day.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔給衣食，事力優重，使於城西之南，治療百姓病。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered food and clothing supplied, with support unusually heavy, and had him treat the people's illnesses south of the western city.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling fed and clothed him lavishly and set him to treat commoners' illnesses south of the western city.

sentences.zh: 懌表諫曰：「臣聞律深惑眾之科，禮絕妖淫之禁，皆所以大明居正，防遏姦邪。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized in remonstrance: "Your servant has heard that the law deeply punishes deluding the masses and the rites utterly forbid demonic lewdness—all to make dwelling in the upright bright and to dam and block wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi remonstrated: "Law punishes deluding the people; rites forbid demonic excess—all to keep the throne upright and bar wickedness.

sentences.zh: 昔在漢末，有張角者，亦以此術熒惑當時。

translations.literal: In old times at the end of Han there was Zhang Jiao, who also used this art to dazzle and bewitch the age.
translations.idiomatic: At Han's end Zhang Jiao had used the same art to bewitch his age.

sentences.zh: 論其所行，與今不異。

translations.literal: Considering what he did, it does not differ from today.
translations.idiomatic: His methods differ in no way from today's.

sentences.zh: 遂能詃誘生人，致黃巾之禍，天下塗炭數十年間，角之由也。

translations.literal: He could thereby seduce living men and bring the calamity of the Yellow Scarves; for decades the realm was scorched—that was Jiao's doing.
translations.idiomatic: He seduced the living and brought the Yellow Scarves; for decades the realm burned—that was Jiao.

sentences.zh: 昔新垣姦，不登於明堂；

translations.literal: In old times the adulterer Xinyuan did not ascend the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Of old the adulterer Xinyuan never reached the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 五利僥，終嬰於顯戮。」

translations.literal: Wuli the opportunist in the end suffered the manifest execution."
translations.idiomatic: Wuli the opportunist died by public execution."

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以懌肅宗懿叔，德先具瞻，委以朝政，事擬周霍。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Yi was Suzong's honored younger uncle and his virtue was foremost before all eyes, entrusted him with court government, his affairs modeled on the Duke of Zhou and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, seeing Yi as Xiaoming's honored uncle and a man all eyes followed, entrusted government to him on the model of Zhou Gong and Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 懌竭力匡輔，以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Yi strove with all his strength to support and correct, taking the realm as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yi labored to steady the state and took the realm as his charge.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉，太后之妹夫也，恃寵驕盈。

translations.literal: Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha, the empress dowager's sister's husband, relied on favor and was arrogant to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha, the dowager's brother-in-law and commander of the guards, grew insolent on favor.

sentences.zh: 懌裁之以法，每抑黜之，為叉所疾。

translations.literal: Yi restrained him by law and each time demoted and disgraced him; Cha therefore hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi checked him with law and repeatedly humiliated him; Cha came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 叉黨人通直郎宋維希叉旨，[7]告懌謀反，禁懌門下，訊問左右及朝貴，貴人分明，乃得雪釋焉。

translations.literal: A partisan of Cha, Direct-Gate Gentleman Song Wei, pleased to Cha's intent, [7] reported that Yi plotted rebellion; they sealed Yi's Gate and Chamber staff, questioned his attendants and court nobles—the noble accounts were clear, and he was only then cleared and released.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's man Song Wei, eager to please, [7] accused Yi of treason; they sealed his staff and questioned attendants and nobles until the truth cleared him.

sentences.zh: 懌以忠而獲謗，乃鳩集昔忠烈之士，為顯忠錄二十卷，以見意焉。

translations.literal: Yi, loyal yet slandered, thereupon gathered former loyal and fierce men and made Records of Manifest Loyalty in twenty scrolls to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Slandered though loyal, Yi compiled Records of Manifest Loyalty in twenty scrolls to declare his mind.

sentences.zh: 正光元年七月，叉與劉騰逼肅宗於顯陽殿，閉靈太后於後宮，囚懌於門下省，誣懌罪狀，遂害之，時年三十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhenguang, Cha with Liu Teng forced Emperor Suzong in Xianyang Hall, shut Empress Dowager Ling in the rear palace, imprisoned Yi in the Gate and Chamber office, fabricated Yi's crimes, and killed him; he was thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguang, seventh month, Cha and Liu Teng seized Xiaoming in Xianyang Hall, walled the dowager in the rear palace, jailed Yi in the Gate and Chamber office, forged charges, and killed him at thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 朝野貴賤，知與不知，含悲喪氣，驚振遠近。

translations.literal: Court and countryside, noble and common, whether they knew him or not, held grief and lost breath; shock rolled through far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside, knowing him or not, grieved until breath failed; shock rolled far and near.

sentences.zh: 夷人在京及歸，聞懌之喪，為之劈面者數百人。

translations.literal: Barbarians in the capital and those who had returned, hearing of Yi's death, split their faces in mourning—several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians in the capital and those returned, hearing of his death, lacerated their faces in mourning—several hundred men.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷。

translations.literal: Prince Guangping Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Guangping Wang Huai.

translations.literal: 〈The text is deficient.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The text is deficient.〉

sentences.zh: 有魏諸王。

translations.literal: There were princes of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Among the princes of Wei,

sentences.zh: 召入華林別館，禁其出入，令四門博士董徵，授以經傳。

translations.literal: They were summoned into the separate lodge of the Hualin Park, their going out and coming in forbidden, and Four-Gate Academician Dong Zheng was ordered to teach them the classics and transmissions.
translations.idiomatic: they were summoned to the Hualin Park lodge, confined from going abroad, and Four-Gate academician Dong Zheng taught them the classics.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，乃得歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died they were then able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died they were allowed home.

sentences.zh: 汝南王悅，好讀佛經，覽書史。

translations.literal: Prince Runan Yue loved reading Buddhist sutras and perusing books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Runan Wang Yue loved Buddhist sutras and historical books.

sentences.zh: 為性不倫，俶儻難測。

translations.literal: By nature he was unorthodox, untrammeled and hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was erratic, rakish, and unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 悅妃閭氏，即東海公之女也，生一子，不見禮答。

translations.literal: Yue's consort, Lady Lu of the Eastern Sea duke's house, bore one son but received no courteous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Lu, daughter of the Eastern Sea duke, bore a son yet won no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 有崔延夏者，以左道與悅遊，合服仙藥松朮之屬。

translations.literal: There was Cui Yanxia, who by heterodox ways kept company with Yue and together took elixir medicines of pine and zhuyu and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanxia, a man of left-hand ways, joined Yue in taking immortality drugs of pine and atractylodes.

sentences.zh: 時輕與出採芝，宿於城外小人之所。

translations.literal: At times he went out lightly to gather fungus and lodged in commoners' dwellings outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He would slip out to gather fungi and sleep in hovels outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 遂斷酒肉粟稻，唯食麥飯。

translations.literal: He then cut off wine, meat, millet, and rice and ate only wheat porridge.
translations.idiomatic: He renounced wine, meat, millet, and rice and ate only wheat gruel.

sentences.zh: 又絕房中而更好男色。

translations.literal: He also ceased the bedchamber and came to prefer male beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the bedchamber and favored men instead.

sentences.zh: 輕忿妃妾，至加捶撻，同之婢使。

translations.literal: In his temper he resented consorts and concubines, even beating them, treating them like maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: He resented his women, beat them like servants, and treated them as maids.

sentences.zh: 悅之出也，妃住於別第。

translations.literal: When Yue went out his consort lodged in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue traveled his consort stayed in a separate house.

sentences.zh: 靈太后敕檢問之，引入，窮悅事故。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered an inquiry; she was brought in and Yue's conduct was exhaustively examined.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered an inquiry; the consort was brought in and Yue's conduct fully examined.

sentences.zh: 妃病杖伏床蓐，瘡尚未愈。

translations.literal: The consort, sick from the cane, lay prostrate on the bed mat; her sores were not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort, flogged sick, lay on her mat; the wounds had not healed.

sentences.zh: 太后因悅之杖妃，乃下令禁斷。

translations.literal: Because Yue had caned the consort, the empress dowager thereupon ordered the practice forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue had beaten her, the dowager forbade such abuse.

sentences.zh: 令諸親王及三蕃，其有正妃疾患百日已上，皆遣奏聞。

translations.literal: She ordered all imperial princes and the three frontier princedoms that if a principal consort was ill more than a hundred days, all were to memorialize and report.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered every imperial prince and frontier prince: if a principal consort was ill beyond a hundred days, they must report it.

sentences.zh: 若有猶行捶撻，就削封位。

translations.literal: If any still applied the cane, their fief and rank were to be stripped on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who still beat her would lose fief and rank at once.

sentences.zh: 及清河王懌為元叉所害，悅了無讎恨之意，乃以桑落酒候伺之，盡其私佞。

translations.literal: When Qinghe Wang Yi was killed by Yuan Cha, Yue had not the slightest thought of vengeance; he waited on him with mulberry-fall wine and exhausted private flattery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinghe Wang Yi fell to Yuan Cha, Yue bore no grudge; he courted Cha with mulberry-fall wine and shameless flattery.

sentences.zh: 叉大喜，以悅為侍中、太尉。

translations.literal: Cha was greatly pleased and made Yue Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was delighted and made him palace attendant and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 臨拜日，就懌子亶求懌服玩之物，不時稱旨。

translations.literal: On the day of his investiture he went to Yi's son Chan to request Yi's robes and curios; Chan did not promptly please him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of appointment he asked Yi's son Chan for his father's robes and curios; Chan displeased him.

sentences.zh: 乃召亶，杖之百下。

translations.literal: He thereupon summoned Chan and caned him a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Chan and beat him a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 亶居廬未葬，形氣羸弱，暴加威撻，殆至不濟。

translations.literal: Chan was in mourning hut, the burial not yet performed; his form and breath were frail and weak—suddenly subjected to fierce blows, he nearly did not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Chan still mourned unburied, frail in body—sudden blows nearly killed him.

translations.literal: 〈The text is deficient.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The text is deficient.〉

sentences.zh: 仍呼阿兒，親自循撫。

translations.literal: He still called "Little son" and personally stroked and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: He still called "Little son" and comforted him with his own hands.

translations.literal: 〈The text is deficient.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The text is deficient.〉

sentences.zh: 悅為大剉碓置於州門，[9]盜者便欲斬其手。

translations.literal: Yue set a great mortar-pestle at the province gate; [9] for thieves he would at once wish to cut off their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yue placed a great crushing mortar at the province gate; [9] thieves he would have their hands cut off at once.

sentences.zh: 時人懼其無常，能行異事，姦偷畏之而暫息。

translations.literal: People at the time feared his unpredictability and that he could perform strange deeds; thieves and rogues feared him and for a time ceased.
translations.idiomatic: People feared his whims and strange punishments; theft briefly ceased.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮舉兵向洛。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang,

sentences.zh: 既憶入間。

translations.literal: Already he recalled entering among men.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrupt; he may already have hoped to enter Luoyang.

translations.literal: 〈The reading here is doubtful.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Doubtful text; the transmitted line is corrupt.〉

sentences.zh: 俄而聞榮肆毒於河陰，遂南奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: Before long he heard that Rong had wantonly slaughtered at Heyin and thereupon fled south to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he heard Rong's massacre at Heyin and fled south to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍立為魏主，號年更興。

translations.literal: Yan installed him as Wei sovereign and changed the reign title to Gengxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan set him up as Wei ruler under the reign title Gengxing.

sentences.zh: 衍遣其將軍王辯送置於境上，以覬侵逼。

translations.literal: Yan sent his general Wang Bian to escort and place him on the border; [10] thereby to covet invasion and pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent Wang Bian to place him on the border [10] as a lever for invasion.

sentences.zh: 及齊獻武王既誅榮，以悅高祖子，宜承大業，乃令人示意。

translations.literal: When Duke Xianwu of Qi had already killed Rong, because Yue was Emperor Gaozu's son and ought to inherit the great enterprise, he therefore had someone convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: After Duke Xianwu of Qi killed Rong, deeming Yue Gaozu's son fit for the throne, he sent word of his intent.

sentences.zh: 悅既至，清狂如故，動為罪失，不可扶持，乃止。

translations.literal: Yue, having arrived, was wild and unbridled as before; his actions were crimes and failures—he could not be supported, and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yue arrived as reckless as ever; his acts were crimes—he could not be enthroned, and they desisted.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，除大司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the Deposed Emperor's accession he was made grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：庶人險暴之性，自幼而長，終以廢黜，不得其終。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The commoner's dangerous and violent nature grew from childhood; in the end he was deposed and did not attain a proper end.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The commoner's dangerous and violent nature grew from childhood; in the end he was deposed and did not come to a proper end.

sentences.zh: 斯乃硃、均之性，堯、舜不能訓也。

translations.literal: This was the nature of Zhu and Jun; Yao and Shun could not instruct it.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the nature of Zhu and Jun; Yao and Shun could not instruct it.

sentences.zh: 京兆早有令問，晚致顛覆，習於所染，可不慎乎！

translations.literal: Jingzhao early had fair renown, but late came to ruin; habituation to what stains one--can one fail to be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao early won fair renown, but late came to ruin; once habituated to what stains one, can one fail to be cautious!

sentences.zh: 清河器識才譽，以懿親作輔，時鐘屯詖，始遘牆茨之逼。

translations.literal: Qinghe had capacity, insight, talent, and reputation, and as an excellent kinsman served as assistant, but the time fell on hardship and crookedness, and he first met the pressure of the wall-thorns.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe had capacity, insight, talent, and reputation, and as an excellent kinsman served as assistant, but the age fell into hardship and crookedness, and he first met the pressure of the wall-thorns.

sentences.zh: 運屬道消，晚扼凶權之手。

translations.literal: His fortunes belonged to a time when the Way declined, and late he was gripped in the hands of violent power.
translations.idiomatic: His fortunes met a time when the Way declined, and late he was throttled by violent power.

sentences.zh: 悲哉！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 廣平早歲驕盈，汝南性致狂逸，揆其終始，俱不足論。

translations.literal: Guangping was arrogant and full in his early years, and Runan by nature reached wild excess; weighing their ends from their beginnings, both are not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangping was arrogant and full in his early years, and Runan by nature ran to wild excess; judged from beginning to end, neither is worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 而悅以天人所棄，卒嬰猜懼之毒，蓋地逼之尤也。

translations.literal: Yet Yue, abandoned by Heaven and men, finally suffered the poison of suspicion and fear; this was likely the extreme result of being pressed too close by position.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yue, abandoned by Heaven and men, finally suffered the poison of suspicion and fear; this was likely the extreme result of a prince pressed too near the throne.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.
